name: citations
summary: Shows where an AI answer came from — a small chip after each claim, named for its source, that previews it, and an "N sources" list under the answer.
useWhen: An AI answer draws on files, pages or records people may want to check.

alternatives.name: hover-card
alternatives.when: you need a preview on an ordinary link that is not an AI source.

alternatives.name: badge
alternatives.when: you are labelling a category, not pointing to where a claim came from.

rules.do: Put the chip right after the sentence it backs, named for its source.
rules.dont: Collect sources only in a footer — people cannot tell which source backs which claim.

rules.do: Leave the chips and list in neutral ink.
rules.dont: Colour citations with the AI gradient or a status colour — they are references, not AI and not status.

a11y: Each chip is a link (or a button when there is no address) named "Q3 deck, source: Q3 board deck.pdf" (the visible label first, then the full title; "Source: <title>" when there is no label); keyboard focus opens the same preview as hover.

A chip with no address opens its preview when pressed or tapped and keeps it open (a press never closes a preview that hover or focus just opened); pressing it again, pressing Escape, pressing outside, or moving focus away closes it. It tells assistive tech with aria-expanded. A chip with an address stays a link.
Chips are 20px tall, larger than a superscript mark, so they are easy to hit.
The sources pill is a disclosure button with aria-expanded controlling the list.
